questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: A bedside lamp is rated at a maximum of 40 W. In a test it transfers 150 J of energy in 5.0 s. Calculate the power of the lamp and state whether it is operating within its rating.
learning_objectives: E2 Calculate power and efficiency

constraints.text: power must not exceed the 40 W rating

marking.worked_solution: P = E/t = 150/5.0 = 30 W, which is less than 40 W, so within rating.

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: A car of mass 1200 kg travels at 15 m/s. A lorry of mass 8000 kg travels at 2.5 m/s. Calculate the momentum of each vehicle and state which would need the larger average force to stop it in the same time.
learning_objectives: M1 Apply conservation of momentum
F1 Apply Newton's second law F = ma

marking.final_answer: car 18 000 kg m/s; lorry 20 000 kg m/s; the lorry needs the larger force
marking.worked_solution: p(car) = 1200 × 15 = 18 000 kg m/s; p(lorry) = 8000 × 2.5 = 20 000 kg m/s. Same stopping time ⇒ F = Δp/Δt is larger for the lorry.

points.description: Lorry: larger change of momentum in same time needs larger force

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: A climber of mass 55 kg ascends a vertical wall of height 15 m in 50 s. Calculate the climber's gain in gravitational potential energy and the minimum average useful power developed. Take g = 9.8 m/s².
learning_objectives: E1 Calculate gravitational potential and kinetic energy
E2 Calculate power and efficiency

marking.worked_solution: ΔEp = mgh = 55 × 9.8 × 15 = 8085 J; P = ΔEp/t = 8085/50 = 161.7 ≈ 162 W (minimum, as other energy transfers are ignored).

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: During an outdoor concert a drumstick rolls horizontally off the edge of a stage riser 1.25 m above the ground. Ignoring air resistance, calculate the time the drumstick takes to reach the ground. Take g = 9.8 m/s².
learning_objectives: K3 Analyse projectile motion with independent horizontal and vertical components
K1 Use the equations of uniformly accelerated motion

marking.worked_solution: Vertical motion from zero vertical velocity: h = ½gt² ⇒ t = √(2h/g) = √(2.5/9.8) = 0.51 s

points.description: Initial vertical velocity zero / horizontal motion irrelevant

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: Travelling along a straight road at 20 m/s, a driver applies the brakes. The car decelerates uniformly and stops after covering 62 m.
learning_objectives: K1 Use the equations of uniformly accelerated motion
F3 Explain motion using Newton's first law

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the size of the car's deceleration.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find how long the car takes to stop.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain how an icy road surface would affect the stopping distance.

marking.final_answer: (a) 3.2 m/s² (b) 6.2 s (c) less friction on ice, so smaller deceleration and longer distance
marking.worked_solution: (a) a = u²/(2s) = 400/124 = 3.2 m/s² (b) t = u/a = 20/3.23 = 6.2 s (c) Ice reduces friction, so the maximum deceleration is smaller and the car travels further.

points.description: Smaller deceleration so longer stopping distance

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: A 0.50 kg ball is released from rest 3.2 m above level ground. Drag is negligible; use g = 9.8 m/s².
learning_objectives: E1 Calculate gravitational potential and kinetic energy

parts.label: a
parts.text: Determine the decrease in gravitational potential energy during the fall.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the ball at the instant before impact.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State and explain the effect on this impact speed if drag were significant.

marking.final_answer: (a) 15.7 J (b) 7.9 m/s (c) lower: energy is transferred to the surroundings by drag
marking.worked_solution: (a) mgh = 0.50 × 9.8 × 3.2 = 15.68 J. (b) v = √(2gh) = 7.9 m/s. (c) Work done against drag ⇒ less kinetic energy ⇒ lower speed.

points.description: Less kinetic energy so lower speed

questions.subject: Introductory Physics
questions.text: Trolley X (mass 2.0 kg) moves to the right at 3.0 m/s. Trolley Y (mass 1.0 kg) moves to the left at 1.5 m/s. They collide head-on and stick together.
learning_objectives: M1 Apply conservation of momentum
E1 Calculate gravitational potential and kinetic energy

constraints.text: momentum to the right is positive

parts.label: a
parts.text: Taking right as positive, calculate the total momentum before the collision.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Determine the velocity of the trolleys after the collision.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Evaluate whether kinetic energy is conserved in the collision.

marking.final_answer: (a) 4.5 kg m/s (b) 1.5 m/s to the right (c) not conserved: 10.1 J before, 3.4 J after
marking.worked_solution: (a) p = 2.0 × 3.0 + 1.0 × (−1.5) = 4.5 kg m/s. (b) v = 4.5/3.0 = 1.5 m/s to the right. (c) Ek before = 9.0 + 1.125 = 10.1 J; after = ½ × 3.0 × 1.5² = 3.4 J; kinetic energy is not conserved (inelastic).

parts.label: b

marking.final_answer: (a) 1840 W (b) 2.8 × 10^5 J (c) yes: total current 14 A exceeds 13 A
